name: NC Burrata
classification_notes: Wide, simple geometric shapes with a generous x-height place this as a geometric sans built for both display and text.
summary: A wide, bold geometric sans with a generous x-height, built for both headlines and long-form text.
description: NC Burrata takes a simple geometric skeleton and widens it out, pairing a large x-height with small caps and alternate letterforms for extra character in display use. Six weights run from Ultra-light to Bold, each with a slanted rather than a true italic. Reads well as both a logotype face and a workhorse text family.
foundry_blurb: Netvarec describe NC Burrata as a modern sans serif with a wider structure and generous x-height, ensuring high readability for longer texts while its elegant curves add a casual, sophisticated touch in display sizes.

name: NC Fontina
classification_notes: A classic grotesque structure with subtle contrast and mid-century Italian references places this in the grotesque camp rather than geometric or humanist.
summary: A refined grotesque with a mid-century Italian sensibility and a true italic across six weights.
description: NC Fontina combines a classic grotesque skeleton with subtle stroke contrast, nodding to mid-century Italian type design rather than the usual Swiss references. Stylistic alternates let dot accents and selected glyphs switch between square and rounded shapes. Six weights with true italics give it reasonable range for editorial and branding work.
foundry_blurb: Netvarec describe NC Fontina as inspired by the mid-century Italian design aesthetic, combining classic grotesk structure with subtle contrast, with the option to switch dot accents and selected glyphs from square to rounded shapes.

name: NC Kobyla
classification_notes: A reliable, general-purpose serif built for daily use across print and digital places this as a contemporary text serif.
summary: A dependable text serif built for everyday reading across print and digital, without an italic cut.
description: NC Kobyla is the plainer of Netvarec's three families, a workhorse serif designed for readability rather than character. Six weights run from Ultra-light to Bold with a set of alternate letterforms and OpenType features, but there's no italic. Suits editorial and long-form text over display work.
foundry_blurb: Netvarec describe NC Kobyla as a reliable serif font family designed for versatility and readability, perfect for daily use across both print and digital media, with alternative letterforms and OpenType features.
